candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XXI.1. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

Isaac's birth: the Lord visited Sarah as He had said. Ephrem reads the laughter motif (Isaac = yiṣḥaq, 'he laughs') as the joy of fulfilled promise: previous laughter (17:17, 18:12) was incredulous; the laughter encoded in Isaac's name is the joy that follows fulfilment. Tewahedo Marian theology preserves this distinction: Mary's response to annunciation moves from troubled wonder (Lk 1:29) to joyful Magnificat (Lk 1:46-55) — the same incredulity-to-joy pattern.
